subsystem.name: GenericRuntimeObjects
subsystem.responsibility: Miscellaneous runtime object infrastructure: ownership of global session/score/dynamics objects, compiler-generated registration trampolines that fold function-pointer slots into integers through the shared boolean-to-int helper, path-string entry accessors over a default path global, qsort-style float ordering callbacks, linked-list runtime helpers, small byte-flag state mutators, debug time formatting, and runtime global defaults.

summary: DERIVED/GUESS grouping of 47 validated functions in the generic_runtime_objects scope. One DERIVED class is attested by the packet: ScoreDatabase (0x0042DC00) owns the score-slot handle dword_7C7030 and base block dword_7C5728 and deallocates both. One thunk (0x0042DBE0) forwards to the canonical session-struct initializer with the global session buffer at 0x7C56C0, and one (0x00435260) forwards to the dynamics-object initializer with the global at 0x7C7428. A large family of nineteen compiler-generated trampolines (0x0042DBF0, 0x00431C60, 0x00435270, 0x0044C7D0, 0x0044C8F0, 0x0044C9B0, 0x0044CA70, 0x0044CAD0, 0x0044CF50, 0x0044D070, 0x0044D130, 0x0044D1F0, 0x0044D250, 0x0044D730, 0x0044D850, 0x0044D910, 0x0044D9D0, 0x0044DA30, 0x0044DFD0) each read a function-pointer global (mostly nullsub stubs) and route it through the shared helper BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E), returning the 0/1 result. Three no-op stubs (0x0043E881, 0x004470FC, 0x0044A44C) are grouped as runtime stub slots. Four path-string accessors share the shape 'object pointer at this+0, string at obj+0x8, default byte_5EA438' (0x004328C0, 0x004328F0, 0x00432A03, 0x00432A10). Two getters (0x00432A60, 0x00432BEA) return the dword at obj+0x1C through this+0. Two float three-way comparators (0x00448440, 0x0044A130) form an ordering-callback interface. Two linked-list helpers (0x00434290, 0x00448E20) cover string-keyed merge sort and head-slot advancement. The remaining classes are per-function GUESS groupings for byte-flag mutators, the pressure-position clamp state, track-config selection, history-buffer shifting, joint-entry counting, debug time formatting, a dual-field store, a physics-buffer handle slot, and runtime global defaults. Owners were UNKNOWN in the packet except ScoreDatabase (DERIVED); class boundaries are defensible functional groupings, not attested source layout.

function_roles.role: Trivial forwarding thunk: calls SessionStructInit (FUN_0042e320) with &byte_7C56C0 and returns its int result unchanged; no arguments taken, no state touched in this frame.
Compiler-generated trampoline: calls BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E) with the int-cast address of global sub_42DC00 (0x0042DC00) and returns its result.

Score-database deallocator: deallocates the score-slot handle dword_7C7030 via ScoreSlotDeallocator (0x0042DDD0), then frees the base block dword_7C5728 through FreeWrapper_7bcf (0x00587BCF) when non-null; returns the free result (or 0 on the null path).

Maps a normalized double (0.0-1.0) to a clamped integer array index: lower half scales the midpoint this[6] (0x18) by 2*a2, upper half folds the far side this[4] - this[6] - 1 back onto the midpoint, then clamps the output this[5] (0x14) to [0, this[4] - 1]; returns the upper bound this[4] - 1. Called by PressureForceFieldMapping (0x004313C0).
Convenience setter: writes the same byte value a2 into the two consecutive byte fields at offsets 0x1D and 0x1E of the object, then returns the object pointer unchanged.

Clamps a list-selection value for row a2 (positive values clamped to the row maximum, non-positive disabled to 0), notifies the track-configuration system via TrackConfig(this, 4, a2) (0x0042E530), and sets the activation flag at this+0x0 and the change flag at this+0x19A4 to 1 when the selection changed.

FIFO history-buffer shift over two regions: the first (start 0xC8, 16-dword records as 4 groups of 11) and the second (start 0xBC8, 55 records) each shift every record onto its predecessor, discarding the oldest; returns a one-past-end cursor. Called by ValidateVehicleConfigurationFile (0x00433ED0).

State helper (userpurge convention, char in al, byte pointers in ecx/esi): accumulates an input char into the byte counter at a2 and raises the byte flag at a3 to 1, returning the input char unchanged.

Side-effect-free joint-entry counter: scans the 64-byte-strided entry array at this+0x16CC, counting consecutive entries with a non-zero first byte until an empty entry or a cap of seven, returning the count (0..7). Called by sub_475A90 (0x00475A90).

Formats a raw time value into a debug display string with a unit suffix via StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck (0x0058815F): combines register bytes, and on the high-bit path scales a float-lookup value (format spec +0x1CD8, index (_EAX & 0xC) * 4) by dbl_59EA20 and points at the unit suffix (_ECX + 24); selects "%.2f %s" (0x005C3820) when (_ECX + 4) == 1, else scales by dbl_59EA18 and uses "%.3f %s" (0x005C3780).

Allocates a 64-byte block via the operator-new wrapper, hands it to PhysicsBufferAlloc, stores the resulting handle into dword_7C73E0[0] (or 0 on allocation failure), and returns the pointer to the dword_7C73E0 array.
Registration trampoline: calls BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E) with the address of the PhysicsShutdown global (0x00431C70) as its single argument and returns the integer result.
Path accessor: returns the path string pointer at offset 0x8 of the object referenced by this+0x0, falling back to the default path global byte_5EA438 when the pointer is null.

Reports whether the string at array offset 0x8 (reached through this[0]) is empty, substituting the byte_5EA438 default when the pointer is null. Called by PollingLoopWithBranch (0x0046E7F0); structural twin of PathAccessor (0x004328C0).
Constant path accessor: ignores its single argument and returns the address of the global char buffer byte_5EA438.

Truncates the path string at array offset 0x8 (reached through this[0]) to its directory part by writing a null terminator after the last backslash, defaulting to byte_5EA438 when null; always returns 0. Called by PollingLoopWithBranch (0x0046E7F0).

Trivial thiscall getter: reads the pointer at this+0 and returns the DWORD at offset 0x1C (28) of the pointed-to object (likely a vtable-based method pointer / per-state handler). Invoked by ConditionalUpdateOnChangedState (0x0046EFE0).

Recursive merge sort for a singly-linked list (node string pointer at +0, next pointer at +4): counts the list, splits at the midpoint by zeroing the next pointer of the split node, sorts both halves recursively, then merges them in ascending string order via strcmp with a byte_5EA438 fallback for null strings; returns the merged head (or the input unchanged for <2 nodes).

classes.name: ScoreDatabase
classes.responsibility: Owns the score-slot handle (dword_7C7030) and the base score-database block (dword_7C5728); teardown deallocates the slot first and then frees the base block through the shared free wrapper when it is non-null.

classes.name: SessionData
classes.responsibility: Global session structure at 0x7C56C0, initialized through the canonical session-struct init routine via the forwarding thunk 0x0042DBE0.

classes.name: RuntimeRegistrationThunk
classes.responsibility: Family of compiler-generated registration/atexit-style trampolines: each reads a function-pointer global (typically a no-op nullsub stub) and folds it into a 0/1 integer through the shared helper BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E). Grouped by shared call shape, not by attested source identity.

classes.name: RuntimeStubSlot
classes.responsibility: No-op placeholder routines (nullsub_19/20/21) with empty bodies; likely occupy vtable or callback slots. Whether some are disassembly artifacts (data misidentified as code) is unconfirmed.

classes.name: PathEntry
classes.responsibility: Object holding a path/name string pointer at obj+0x8, reached through the object pointer at this+0; the global default string byte_5EA438 substitutes for null pointers. Provides path retrieval, empty-string check, constant path access, and in-place directory truncation.

classes.name: HandlerSlotAccessor
classes.responsibility: Trivial getters that return the DWORD at obj+0x1C of the object pointed to by this+0; likely a per-state handler or vtable pointer. Two structural twins, one invoked by ConditionalUpdateOnChangedState.

classes.name: FloatSortComparator
classes.responsibility: Qsort/bsearch-style three-way float ordering callbacks (return 1/0/-1) over a float key field at +0x4 or +0xC of the compared objects. Grouped by comparator shape; the compared class is unknown.

classes.name: LinkedListRuntime
classes.responsibility: Generic singly-linked-list operations: recursive merge sort of a string-keyed list (string at +0, next at +4) and head-slot advancement over up to 11 list heads (slot count at this+0x18, slots at this+0x1C, node next-link at node+0x1C). Node classes differ between the two operations and are not proven identical.

classes.name: PhysicsBuffer
classes.responsibility: Owns the global physics-buffer handle array at dword_7C73E0; the allocation thunk creates a 64-byte block through the operator-new wrapper and stores a physics-buffer handle (or 0 on failure) into slot 0.

classes.name: DynamicsObject
classes.responsibility: Global dynamics object at 0x7C7428 (typed double by the raw corpus but serving as an object handle), initialized through the canonical dynamics-object init routine via the forwarding thunk 0x00435260.

classes.name: PositionRangeState
classes.responsibility: Object holding a range bound (this+0x10), midpoint (this+0x18) and output index (this+0x14); converts a normalized pressure/force-field position into a clamped grid index for PressureForceFieldMapping.

classes.name: StateByteMutator
classes.responsibility: Small byte-level state mutators grouped by shape, not by proven common class: dual byte setter (0x1D/0x1E), counter-accumulate-plus-flag helper (a2/a3 pointer outputs), and single byte-flag clear (0x1C59). The three functions operate on heterogeneous objects.

classes.name: TrackConfigSelection
classes.responsibility: Track-configuration selection state: a row-stride selection array (row maximum at 0xBC0, selection at 0xBC4 within the 64-byte row stride), an activation/dirty flag at this+0x0, a selection-change flag at this+0x19A4, and notification of the track-configuration system via TrackConfig(this, 4, row).

classes.name: HistoryBuffer
classes.responsibility: FIFO history buffer over two 16-dword-record regions of the struct: 44 records at 0xC8 (shifted as 4 groups of 11) and 55 records at 0xBC8; every call shifts each record onto its predecessor, discarding the oldest.

classes.name: DynamicsJointEntryTable
classes.responsibility: Table of 64-byte-strided joint entries at this+0x16CC; an active entry has a non-zero first byte, and the counter scans consecutive active entries up to a cap of seven.

classes.name: DebugTimeFormatter
classes.responsibility: Formats a raw time value into a debug display string with a unit suffix using two shared literal format strings ("%.2f %s" / "%.3f %s"), two scale doubles, and a format-spec object (selector dword at +4, unit-suffix string at +0x18, float lookup table at +0x1CD8).

classes.name: TwinValueStore
classes.responsibility: Fastcall dual-field store writing the same DWORD into target offsets 0x58 and 0x5C on every call (both fields are overwritten each invocation); possibly twin caches or a logical pair kept as two DWORDs.

classes.name: RuntimeGlobalDefaults
classes.responsibility: Straight-line reset of two runtime globals together: float flt_7CD160 to 0.0 and dword dword_7CD164 to the literal 1065353216 (the IEEE-754 single-precision bit pattern of 1.0f, DERIVED interpretation).

interfaces.name: OrderingPredicate
interfaces.purpose: Three-way float ordering callback (returns 1 when the first argument's key field sorts greater, 0 when equal, -1 when smaller), consistent with qsort/bsearch-style ordering callbacks over heterogeneous key offsets (+0x4, +0xC).

compatibility_contracts.name: ScoreDatabaseTeardown
compatibility_contracts.description: The score database must expose a deallocation path that releases the score-slot handle (dword_7C7030) through the slot deallocator before freeing the base block (dword_7C5728) via the shared free wrapper; only a non-null base block is freed, and the free result (or 0) is returned.

compatibility_contracts.name: SessionStructInit
compatibility_contracts.description: A global session structure must exist at 0x7C56C0 and be initialized through the canonical session-init routine; callers reach it through the forwarding thunk 0x0042DBE0, which returns the init routine's int result unchanged.

compatibility_contracts.name: RegistrationThunkHelper
compatibility_contracts.description: A shared boolean-to-int helper at 0x00587B3E is used by registration-style trampolines to fold a function-pointer slot (typically a no-op nullsub stub) into a 0/1 integer; the registration thunk family must preserve this helper call contract, returning the helper's result directly.

compatibility_contracts.name: DefaultPathFallback
compatibility_contracts.description: An application default path buffer at 0x5EA438 is used as the fallback string whenever a path/name entry (object pointer at this+0, string at obj+0x8) holds a null pointer; accessors substitute it, and one accessor mutates the returned buffer in place to truncate the path to its directory part.

compatibility_contracts.name: PhysicsBufferHandleSlot
compatibility_contracts.description: A global physics-buffer handle array at 0x7C73E0 holds the handle produced from a 64-byte operator-new block; slot 0 is written with the handle (or 0 on allocation failure) and the array pointer is returned to the caller.

compatibility_contracts.name: TrackConfigNotify
compatibility_contracts.description: A list-selection change must clamp the requested selection to the row maximum (or disable to 0 for non-positive requests), notify the track-configuration system via TrackConfig(this, 4, row), and raise the activation flag at this+0x0 and the selection-change flag at this+0x19A4 only when the selection actually changes.

compatibility_contracts.name: TimeFormatLiterals
compatibility_contracts.description: Time formatting uses two shared literal format strings, "%.2f %s" (0x5C3820) and "%.3f %s" (0x5C3780), plus two scale doubles (0x59EA20, 0x59EA18); a format-spec object supplies a selector dword at +4, a unit-suffix string at +0x18, and a float lookup table at +0x1CD8. A replacement display path must preserve these strings and the selector semantics to keep debug output byte-identical.

compatibility_contracts.name: GlobalDefaultsReset
compatibility_contracts.description: Two runtime defaults are reset together by a straight-line initializer: float flt_7CD160 to 0.0 and dword dword_7CD164 to 1065353216 (the IEEE-754 single-precision bit pattern of 1.0f, DERIVED interpretation).

unresolved: PositionIndexClamp (0x0042E290): globals dbl_59E420 (0x0059E420) and dbl_59E880 (0x0059E880) are flagged by packet facts as read but appear nowhere in the raw decompiled source; the skeleton fill names BaseDoubleConstant and HalfStep, neither verifiable from this packet.

TimeFormatStringForDebugDisplay (0x004319DA): register-byte arithmetic (BYTE1(_ECX) + _EAX), the a3 + 1149962476 counter offset (Hex-Rays artifact of an unknown base), the uninitialized v7 on the fallthrough path, and the double-scaling of the already-scaled value when the +4 field check fails all remain semantically unclear.

StateFlagSetter (0x0042ED44): the a2/a3/a4/a5/a6 prototype split is a decompiler guess (positive sp value detected in raw source); whether a2 is a running counter and a3 a persistent flag needs caller confirmation.
BooleanToIntConversion (0x00587B3E): behavior is unknown from this packet - it is unclear whether it invokes the passed function pointer or merely folds its numeric value into a 0/1 integer.

nullsub stubs (0x0043E881, 0x004470FC, 0x0044A44C): whether these addresses are genuine empty functions or disassembly artifacts (data/padding misidentified as code) is unconfirmed; nullsub_20's far-return (retfw 0FFFFh) and 63 declared parameters are unexplained.
forwarder_to_sub_447780 (0x00447774): the identity and semantics of the forwarded target sub_447780 are not established by this packet.

ScoreDatabaseDeallocator (0x0042DC00): dword_7C7030 is read but never null-checked before being passed to ScoreSlotDeallocator; whether that deallocator tolerates a null handle is unverified. The caller-side meaning of the returned free result is unknown (no callers in packet).

LinkedListMergeSortRecursive (0x00434290): node ownership/allocation is not visible in the packet; the purpose of byte_5EA438 as the fallback string and the meaning of the sorted keys depend on the directory-enumeration caller.

LinkedListNodeTraversal (0x00448E20): the layout of the pointed-to node is inferred only from usage (next link at node+0x1C); the clamp to 11 suggests a fixed 11-element slot array but its capacity is not proven.
HistoryBufferShift (0x0042EBC0): the semantic meaning of the shifted history records is unknown (4 groups of 11 at 0xC8, 55 at 0xBC8); call context unknown (no static path from tick root).
DynamicsJointCount (0x00431820): the layout of each 64-byte joint entry is undefined beyond its first byte; the zero first-byte sentinel's meaning is not defined.

Thunk_1bc0 (0x00431BC0): OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper and PhysicsBufferAlloc are named in the raw source but absent from the packet callee list; whether the alloc consumes the operator-new block in place or copies is not established.

DynamicsObjectInitializationThunk (0x00435260): the canonical target FUN_00438c10 is absent from the packet callee list; dbl_7C7428 is typed double by the raw corpus but serves as an object handle, and its real layout is not evidenced.
SessionStructInitThunk (0x0042DBE0): the canonical target FUN_0042e320 is absent from the packet callee list; the contents and layout of the 0x7C56C0 global buffer are not evidenced.
ResetGlobalDefaults (0x0044CCF4): the decimal literal 1065353216 equals the IEEE-754 single-precision bit pattern of 1.0f, but that interpretation is DERIVED and not stated in the packet evidence.

TrackConfigSelection (0x0042EB60): the meaning of the row-stride group (TrackConfig group argument 4) and the row-maximum field require the caller's row schema; the offsets 3008/0xBC0 and 3012/0xBC4 are stated in packet prose (source:raw only) and are not independently corroborated, and no packet field evidence ref exists for them, so they are not declared as class fields.

Dropped class-field declarations (LinkedListRuntime head_slot_array at this+0x1C, TrackConfigSelection row_maximum/row_selection at 0xBC0/0xBC4, DebugTimeFormatter FormatSpec +4/+0x18/+0x1CD8): these offsets appear only in decompiled-source prose in the packet, which carries no matching field evidence ref for them, so declaring them as class fields would violate the evidence-ref contract; their semantics remain described in the class responsibilities and function roles.

PathEntry family: the contents and initialization site of the byte_5EA438 buffer are not evidenced; the object behind this+0 and the meaning of its +0x8 element are unnamed, inferred from dereferences.

GetStructDwordAt0x1C pair (0x00432A60, 0x00432BEA): identity of the target structure and the meaning of the DWORD at obj+0x1C depend on the caller ConditionalUpdateOnChangedState (0x0046EFE0), not visible in this packet.
DualFieldStore (0x004485C5): the purpose of storing the same value into both 0x58 and 0x5C is unknown; a3 is never referenced and may be vestigial.
FloatSortComparator pair (0x00448440, 0x0044A130): the semantic meaning of the compared float keys (+0x4, +0xC) and the compared object classes are unknown; no static callers are recorded.

StringLogDeallocate (0x0044C7D0) and the other nullsub-wrapping thunks: whether BooleanToIntConversion invokes the passed pointer or merely tests its value is not established; the wrapped stubs have no executable bodies, so their intended behavior is unrecoverable from this packet.

The atexit/registration interpretation of the AtexitHandlerRegistration names (0x00431C60, 0x0044CA70, 0x0044D1F0, 0x0044D9D0) rests only on the legacy ABI labels; no registration-table or atexit evidence is present in the packet.
